title: Taiwan Creative Content Fest Opens as Chair Sue Wang Says ‘Culture Is Power’ Amid AI Shift
description: Sue Wang, chair of the Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA), opened the seventh Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF) in Taipei on Friday by sayin
body:
Sue Wang, chair of the Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA), opened the seventh Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF) in Taipei on Friday by saying artificial intelligence is reshaping how the creative industries, and even human society, are defined.

	“We are all asking: Does cultural content still have a future?” Wang said.

	She said AI could take on technical tasks but could not replace the elements of creative work that move people. Wang urged Taiwan to put its technology strengths to work in ways that serve people and improve their lives. “I hope more people believe that culture is power. Especially in this rapidly changing era, cultural content can help create a happier society,” she said.
	

	Wang also called this year’s edition an important milestone for the industry. “Everyone is working hard to build partnerships and integration, both horizontally and vertically. Cross-sector, cross-platform and cross-border collaboration has become a trend,” she said.

	The event features 107 Market exhibitors from seven countries and 92 project and story pitches spanning film, series, animation, documentaries, publishing and comics. Industry participants from 28 countries are attending. The four-day Forum will hold 12 sessions with more than 20 speakers, addressing international co-production, streaming-platform consolidation, IP, short-form content and AI.

	Hosted by Taiwanese actor Allison Lin, the opening ceremony was attended by Culture Minister Li Yuan; Wang Ting-an, executive secretary of the National Development Fund under the Executive Yuan; Weta FX CEO Daniel Seah; Toei Company President and CEO Yoshimura Fumio; Frédéric Laplanche, director of the French Office in Taipei; Fernando Mariano Schmidt Hernández, director of the Chilean Trade Office in Taipei; and Marco Lombardi of the Italian Economic, Trade and Cultural Promotion Office in Taipei, among many other local and international luminaries.
	

	Li, who chaired the evaluation committee at TCCF’s first edition, said he had watched the event grow from an exhibition into a market and an international platform. “Now we’re thinking about the future of Taiwan’s cultural content ecosystem and how TCCF can become an Asian creative-content brand, helping cultural workers across Asia and around the world find opportunities and funding. That is one of the key goals behind the Ministry of Culture and TAICCA,” he said.

	TCCF runs Nov. 6-9 at Taipei Nangang Exhibition Center, Hall 2.

schema.headline: Taiwan Creative Content Fest Opens as Chair Sue Wang Says ‘Culture Is Power’ Amid AI Shift

title: Pamela Abdy on Life After Warner Bros: ‘Right Now, I’m Taking a Break and Chilling’
description: A month after her departure from Warner Bros. was announced, Pamela Abdy made her first industry appearance Thursday night at the Women in Film Hon
body:
A month after her departure from Warner Bros. was announced, Pamela Abdy made her first industry appearance Thursday night at the Women in Film Honors at the Beverly Hilton.

	On the morning of Oct. 1, Abdy was announced as WIF’s inaugural Vanguard Award recipient. Then, she was serving as co-chair and CEO of Warner Bros. Motion Picture Group with her longtime producing partner Michael DeLuca. Later that night, Abdy and DeLuca learned that would not usher the film studio into its next chapter amid the Skydance merger. Just over a month later, she was ready to talk about it.
	

	“Right now, I’m taking a break and chilling,” Abdy told Variety‘s Marc Malkin on the red carpet. 

	“I got to go see every single one of my daughter’s volleyball games, without being interrupted. So that’s what I’m doing right now,” she said. 

	When Malkin asked her about the swirling rumors about her next stop, including the idea that she and De Luca could fill the open film head job at Netflix, Abdy said, “When I decide what I’m doing, I promise I will tell everyone. But honestly, it’s an interesting time to be able to take a break, and really decide what I want.

	“I know what happiness is when I’m working with filmmakers, and wherever and whatever I end up doing, that’s my goal is to continue to work with the best storytellers out there,” Abdy said.

	When Malkin asked if she thinks the new combined company can reach its goal of releasing 30 movies a year, Abdy replied, “I don’t know. I’m not there. I hope they do.”

	The WIF prize recognizes the breadth of Abdy’s career beyond Warner Bros., where she oversaw blockbusters and award darlings including “One Battle After Another,” “Sinners,” “Barbie,” “Weapons,” and “Dune: Part Two.” Last year, Warner Bros. tied the all-time studio record with 11 Academy Awards from an industry-leading 30 nominations. That said, not all of the duo’s big-budget swings paid off. For example, “The Bride!” lost $100 million theatrically after failing to spark at the box office this spring. Then, “Digger,” Warner Bros.’ final release as a standalone studio, proved to be one of the biggest financial misfires of the year.
	

	WIF is also honoring Adria Arjona, Beth de Araújo, Gemma Chan and Salma Hayek Pinault at Thursday’s gala.

schema.headline: Pamela Abdy on Life After Warner Bros: ‘Right Now, I’m Taking a Break and Chilling’

title: ‘Pout-Pout Fish’ Studio Like a Photon Creative Unveils Seven-Film Animation Slate With Sola Media, Ahead of AFM (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Like a Photon Creative, the Australian animation studio behind “The Pout-Pout Fish,” has lined up seven new animated features and handed internatio
body:
Like a Photon Creative, the Australian animation studio behind “The Pout-Pout Fish,” has lined up seven new animated features and handed international distribution rights on the full slate to Sola Media.

	Production finance comes from Elevate Production Finance and Alceon Entertainment Partners. Maslow Entertainment has picked up Australia and New Zealand distribution on the features. According to the companies, the lineup could create as many as 1,000 jobs in Australia and Ireland. Like a Photon Creative CEO Kristen Souvlis will attend the upcoming American Film Market (AFM).
	

	First up is “Familiar,” an original developed in-house that will be made as a treaty co-production with Irish company Elephant Goldfish. Production on the film is expected to start in March 2027. Further titles will be revealed later.

	The film is set at Ironclaw Academy, a school where the animal companions of sorcerers – known as familiars – go through a demanding and frequently messy training regime. Its central character is Josie, a feisty young cat.

	“Families keep coming back to our films, and we’re focused on making projects that deserve that trust, with strong stories and broad appeal. ‘Familiar’ is the first of seven new features in our growing pipeline. Sola Media has a proven track record with our work, and together we see real opportunity to take Australian and European content to international audiences,” Souvlis said.

	Alongside each of the seven features, the studio will make short-form direct-to-consumer material built from footage that won’t appear in the films themselves. That content will be bundled with the movies and rolled out across a range of online and social platforms.
	

	The slate follows “The Pout-Pout Fish,” which Sola Media handled internationally. Adapted from the popular children’s book series, the film opened at No. 9 at the U.S. box office and currently ranks as the fourth highest-grossing Australian film of 2026. It also hit No. 1 on Amazon Prime Kids and No. 6 among all Prime viewers. Maslow released it in Australian cinemas on Jan. 1, with Viva Kids handling the U.S. release on March 20.

	Sola Media will also oversee international distribution for the studio’s next release, “The Neverending Pillow Fort,” the first feature from Crayola Studios, produced with MIMO Studios. Allison Brownmoore directs the film, which is due in early 2027. Elizabeth Cullen and Sofia Rose voice best friends Maggie and Abby, with Guy Pearce, David Tennant, Teresa Palmer and Marsai Martin also in the cast.

	Sola Media managing director Solveig Langeland said mixing humor and heart has always sat at the center of the studio’s storytelling, backed by its skill at bringing characters to life through strong voice casts. “We are proud of the successes we have achieved together and excited to embark on the next chapter of our partnership. With their expansion into co-productions with Ireland, Like a Photon is taking another exciting step forward. Their forward-thinking approach to building brands and engaging audiences through direct-to-consumer content from the earliest stages of production adds a powerful new dimension to their upcoming slate, creating awareness and marketing momentum long before the films reach cinemas,” she said.

	Separately, Like a Photon Creative has teamed with Screen Queensland on the Escalate: Feature Focus Writers Initiative. Under the scheme, six screenwriters based in Queensland will each write a script for a possible 3D animated feature, working from concepts supplied by the studio. Writers’ rooms kick off in February 2027.

	The studio has backed and made 10 animated features in 3D for worldwide theatrical release since 2017, among them “The Wishmas Tree,” “Combat Wombat” and its 2023 sequel, “Daisy Quokka: World’s Scariest Animal,” “The Sloth Lane” and “The Lost Tiger.” It also created the Sanctuary City multiverse for Universal Content Group.

	Langeland founded Sola Media in 2004. The company, which has offices in Stuttgart and Munich, was acquired in 2020 by Embracer Group’s Plaion but continues to operate independently under Langeland and fellow managing director Moritz Peters.

title: ‘Lord of the Rings,’ ‘Avatar’ VFX House Weta FX to Invest in Taiwan’s Moonshine Studio Under AI Pact With TAICCA
description: Weta FX, the New Zealand visual effects company behind “The Lord of the Rings” and “Avatar,” will invest in Taiwanese animation and VFX outfit Moon
body:
Weta FX, the New Zealand visual effects company behind “The Lord of the Rings” and “Avatar,” will invest in Taiwanese animation and VFX outfit Moonshine Studio. 

	The investment is part of a partnership with the Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA) aimed at making Taiwan an AI hub for Asia’s content industries.

	Weta FX CEO Daniel Seah and TAICCA chair Sue Wang signed a memorandum of understanding on Friday at Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF) in Taipei. Taiwan’s Minister of Culture Li Yuan attended the signing. No figure was given for the investment.
	

	Seah said the partnership has three parts. The first is the investment in Moonshine, founded by Lin Chia-chi, which he said had been around six months in the making. The second is a technology platform that will invest in Taiwanese film and TV projects and use Weta FX’s global reach to get them in front of wider audiences.

	“On the AI road, nobody is really far, far ahead,” Seah said. “We all have to venture into this tech-filled AI world together. That’s why, while investing in Taiwan, we’re investing in technology.”

	The third part, and the one Seah said he values most, is talent. A program will allow Taiwanese filmmakers, particularly young ones, to come to Weta FX for exchanges and internships, and potentially to work there in future.

	Seah has spent close to 16 years as a VFX CEO. That includes 14 years running Digital Domain, the company co-founded by James Cameron. He moved to Peter Jackson’s Weta FX nearly two years ago. Li noted that Seah was born in Malaysia and grew up in New Taipei’s Yonghe district before working in China and Hong Kong.
	

	Weta FX’s staff alone, Seah said, make up around 2% of the population of Wellington, New Zealand’s capital.

	“Over the past 30 years, Weta turned Wellington from a political capital into such an important global production base,” Seah said. “We think Taiwan has even more of that opportunity.”

	Wang said Moonshine’s team ranked first among Taiwan’s VFX houses. “Every time we met the Moonshine team, my only worry was: Can you make money like this? How long can you keep going?” she said. Wang added that the team “deserves to be put to better use, and seen by more people.”

	Wang also thanked Taiwan’s National Development Fund for its support.

	Li summed up the day in an eight-character Chinese phrase, “Daniel Seah comes home, dreams come true.” The phrase plays on Moonshine’s Chinese name, which means “dream.” He said AI and cultural technology will be among the Ministry of Culture’s priorities for the next four years.

	Li joined Wang Film Productions at 37 hoping to make original animation, and gave up two to three years later. “I thought maybe this dream would take 20 or 30 years to come true,” he said. “I didn’t expect that after waiting so long, I would at least see it come true with my own eyes.”

	Also on hand were TAICCA president Erica Wang and three Weta FX executives: chief technology officer Kimball Thurston, VFX supervisor Sean Noel Walker and R&D head Andrew Moffat.

schema.headline: ‘Lord of the Rings,’ ‘Avatar’ VFX House Weta FX to Invest in Taiwan’s Moonshine Studio Under AI Pact With TAICCA

title: Salon.com Shuts Down Cultural and Political Site After 31 Years
description: Salon.com, the website that became popular in the early days of the internet offering cultural commentary, progressive political analysis, lifestyl
body:
Salon.com, the website that became popular in the early days of the internet offering cultural commentary, progressive political analysis, lifestyle content and more, is shutting down, the company announced Thursday. 

	“When Salon launched in November 1995, the web was a very different place. A small group of journalists set out to create something original: a publication with a strong voice, a curiosity about the world and a belief that the internet could bring journalism and readers together in new ways. They helped pioneer a form of journalism that would come to define an entirely new era of publishing,” the editorial team wrote in a statement. 
	

	The San Francisco-based site was known for launching numerous writers’ careers and was a daily stop for many readers in the days before social media. Among the film critics that wrote for Salon were Stephanie Zacharek, Andrew O’Hehir and Charles Taylor. The site’s television writers and critics included Heather Havrilesky, Hanh Nguyen, Maureen Ryan and Melanie McFarland.

	Salon joins later-arriving sites such as Buzzfeed and Gawker that found it difficult to monetize cultural and topical reporting for a general audience and eventually shut down. 

	“The business realities of independent digital journalism have changed profoundly over the years,” the editors continued in their statement. “After careful consideration, we have reached the difficult decision that our publishing model is no longer sustainable. We know this news will be deeply disappointing to many of you, and we share that sadness.

	“Thirty-one years is a remarkable run, but what matters most is what happened during those years: the journalism, the ideas, the voices, the conversations and the community that grew around them. Salon helped demonstrate what digital journalism could be and could become. We hope that legacy will continue to matter long after today.
	

	“Thank you for being part of our story. It has been an extraordinary privilege,” the statement concluded.

schema.headline: Salon.com Shuts Down Cultural and Political Site After 31 Years

title: Priyanka Chopra Jonas, Russell Crowe Sci-Fi Thriller ‘Bluefly’ Adds ‘Beast’ Star Daniel MacPherson (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Daniel MacPherson, who recently starred opposite Russell Crowe in “Beast,” has signed on for “Bluefly,” a science-fiction action thriller toplined
body:
Daniel MacPherson, who recently starred opposite Russell Crowe in “Beast,” has signed on for “Bluefly,” a science-fiction action thriller toplined by Crowe and Priyanka Chopra Jonas. 

	“Predators” filmmaker Nimród Antal is directing.

	MacPherson will play Dugan, a Special Forces soldier toughened by years of combat, joining the film’s two leads.


	The film unfolds in the Congo. Chopra Jonas plays a U.N. translator, still mourning a loss, who gets pulled into a secret operation to retrieve an enigmatic aircraft that has gone down.
	

	The script comes from David Frigerio (“Beast”), William Eubank (“Underwater”) and Carlyle Eubank (“Muzzle”). The casting brings MacPherson back together with both Crowe and Frigerio following “Beast,” the mixed martial arts action film in which the two actors shared the screen and which Frigerio wrote.

	Michael Jefferson is producing through Polite Society, alongside Frigerio via Broken Open Pictures, Deborah Glover of G2 Dispatch, Highland Film Group’s Arianne Fraser and Delphine Perrier, and Vanessa Yao Guo. Guy Davies, RuthAnne Frigerio, Brian Kavanaugh-Jones, Jason Kringstein, Katie Leary, Scott Levenson and James Norbury serve as executive producers.

	Cameras are set to roll shortly on Australia’s Gold Coast, where principal photography on the Congo-set story will take place.

	Beyond “Beast,” MacPherson’s big-screen résumé includes “Land of Bad,” “Poker Face,” “A Wrinkle in Time,” “The Osiris Child” and “Infini.” His TV work spans “Foundation,” “Strike Back,” “APB” and “The Shannara Chronicles,” giving him a long track record in action and genre fare across both film and series.
	

	MacPherson is represented by Entertainment 360, Buchwald and Benchmark Creative.

title: Helene Hahn Loyd, Executive With Disney and DreamWorks, Dies at 78
description: Helene Hahn Loyd, the executive who was part of the executive team that built DreamWorks SKG and was instrumental in Disney’s renaissance of the 19
body:
Helene Hahn Loyd, the executive who was part of the executive team that built DreamWorks SKG and was instrumental in Disney’s renaissance of the 1980s and ’90s, died Oct. 24 in Park City,  Utah. She was 78.

	Born Helene Bulakoff in Westbury, New York, she graduated from Hofstra University and moved to Los Angeles. She started her career with a temp job at Paramount Pictures while she was attending law school, and earned her degree from Loyola Law School in 1975.
	

	Returning to Paramount, she rose to senior vice president and earned a reputation as a formidable dealmaker. At Walt Disney Studios, she was named executive vice president in 1981, becoming one of the most high-ranking women in the film business at the time.

	Working with Jeffrey Katzenberg, she helped engineer the studio’s comeback, including its partnership with Pixar. In 1994, she was recruited to help build DreamWorks SKG, and served as its chief operating officer. 

	She was a passionate mentor to upcoming female executives. 

	After moving to Park City, she “approached skiing with the same ferocity she applied to dealmaking,” her official obit stated. 

	Her husband of over two decades, Charles “Chuck” Loyd Jr., died in July.

	Donations may be made to U.S. Ski & Snowboard, honoring their shared love of skiing and their commitment to supporting the next generation of athletes. Please indicate that your gift is made in their memory.

schema.headline: Helene Hahn Loyd, Executive With Disney and DreamWorks, Dies at 78

title: Jalen Brunson Makes ‘Law & Order: SVU’ Acting Debut as a Promoted Cop: ‘I Focused on My Goals… Things Worked Out’
description: Jalen Brunson, who led the New York Knicks to their first NBA championship in 53 years in June, guest starred as a cop in Thursday’s episode of “La
body:
Jalen Brunson, who led the New York Knicks to their first NBA championship in 53 years in June, guest starred as a cop in Thursday’s episode of “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit.”

	He appears in the episode for one brief scene, meeting up with Mariska Hargitay‘s Olivia Benson to provide information on a suspect he’d had a run-in with in the past. When they first sit down together at a café, she compliments him on his recent promotion to detective after serving as a beat cop.
	

	“Detective Madison! Look at you out of uniform, huh? Congratulations on the promotion,” she says to him. He thanks her, then makes a clear meta-reference to his work on the basketball court: “I focused on my goals, gave 110% — things worked out.” Smiling, Benson replies, “Yeah, they did.”

	Detective Madison then briefs Brunson on his experience with the suspect, providing information that allows her to eventually get the search warrant she needs to solve the case of the week, which involves the sexual assault of a 16-year-old girl. The scene lasts for about one minute.



	

					Jalen Brunson as Detective Jay Madison in “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit.”
									Virginia Sherwood/NBC
	



	Hargitay, who executive produces “SVU” in addition to starring, is a big Knicks fan who is frequently seen courtside when the team plays at Madison Square Garden. “I want everyone to throw out every book on leadership they have and replace it with a photo of Jalen,” she told Variety in June. “We have so much to learn from his brand of strength.” Hargitay and Brunson have become friends, and when asked what he’d do next after winning the championship earlier this year, he joked that he’d “try to get on ‘SVU.'”

schema.headline: Jalen Brunson Makes ‘Law & Order: SVU’ Acting Debut as a Promoted Cop: ‘I Focused on My Goals… Things Worked Out’

title: Foot Fetish Encounter Leaves a Body in the Freezer in Singapore Dark Comedy Taiwan Creative Content Fest Project ‘Build to Order’
description: A young Singaporean couple who sell pictures of the wife’s feet online end up with a corpse in their freezer in “Build to Order,” the debut feature
body:
A young Singaporean couple who sell pictures of the wife’s feet online end up with a corpse in their freezer in “Build to Order,” the debut feature from director Huang Junxiang, which is at the Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF) in Taipei this week.

	Singaporean couple Penny and Allan both work in real estate. They wed young so they could get a public housing flat, but property prices that keep climbing still leave them strapped. To bring in extra money, they put photos of Penny’s feet up for sale online. Then a rich client with a foot fetish offers them a staggering amount for the chance to suck her toes face to face, and they say yes.
	

	The meeting goes badly wrong. The man suffers an allergic reaction, Allan’s amateur attempt at first aid fails and the client dies. In a panic, the couple stash him in their freezer. Months on, his widow, who has no idea what happened, taps them to list her luxury mansion – drawing the pair ever deeper into greed and guilt as they scramble to save themselves.

	“When I was looking to buy my first home in Singapore, every property agent I met warned me that making the wrong decision would cost me financially in the long haul,” Huang says. “They said that I can’t make an emotional decision, I needed to make a logical one. In an expensive society like Singapore, I feel that many decisions are made rationally, at the cost of our identities and our relationships.”

	The film is now in post-production, and Huang says finishing it has his full attention.

	“I hope our audiences will be entertained by this dark comedy with genre moments and think a little more about the choices they make and the lives they want to lead,” he says.
	

	Producer Macarius Chia says the film deals with a subject that resonates around the world – housing prices and what it costs to get by. “We were also entertained by the humorous script which takes the story in a few surprising directions, without losing sight of the character’s journey.”

	Executive producer Lim Teck says he believes in Huang’s vision and that the film could become a breakout hit out of Singapore, “where housing and climbing the social ladder are always such hot topics.” Lim adds that the film is reasonably budgeted and has commercial potential.

	In Taipei, the team wants to raise gap financing to finish post, along with partners for audio post and color grading. Chia says they also hope to find “a like-minded international sales agent who believes in the project as the story is accessible.”

	For Lim, TCCF is a chance to introduce the project to friends across Asia’s film industry. “We believe our film has a chance to travel and do well in various Asian markets,” he says.

	The Taiwan Creative Content Fest, organized by the Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA), runs Nov. 6–9 at the Taipei Nangang Exhibition Center.

title: Rosamund Pike Set to Star in and Produce ‘Feed’, Body Horror Movie From Leslye Headland
description: Rosamund Pike will star in and produce “Feed,” a new body horror movie from “The Acolyte” director Leslye Headland and screenwriter Daniella Isaacs
body:
Rosamund Pike will star in and produce “Feed,” a new body horror movie from “The Acolyte” director Leslye Headland and screenwriter Daniella Isaacs.

	Inspired by the 2022 Finnish horror movie “Hatching,” the official logline for “Feed” reads: “When a desperate mother discovers an obscure collagen supplement that promises to make her tween gymnast daughter an influencer star, the fame and success they crave come fast. But as her daughter goes viral, she begins a monstrous transformation.”
	

	“Long have I wanted to make a film that plays anarchically with our obsession with social media and self-improvement, our desire for fame without notable admirable skill and, let’s put it out there, the monstrosity of modern motherhood,” Pike said. “‘Feed’ deals with all these things.” 

	Pike will produce through her Primitive Streak banner. Other producers include Shelley Browning for Magnolia Entertainment, Steven Schneider for Spooky Pictures, Ara Keshishian and Petr Jakl for ZQ Entertainment and Sam Ritzenberg for Agile Films. ZQ Entertainment financed development on the project. The Veterans will represent the international sales rights, with CAA Media Finance handling the United States. Sales will commence at the American Film Market next week.

	“Daniella’s script is audacious, disturbing and deeply human and Rosamund is among the boldest actors working today,” Headland added. “I couldn’t ask for better partners to take on the darker corners of this story and I feel incredibly lucky to be making this film with two women whose work I admire so much.” 
	

	Pike, best known for her roles in “Gone Girl,” “Pride & Prejduice” and “Die Another Day,” was last seen in Guy Ritchie’s action comedy “In the Grey” alongside Henry Cavill and Jake Gyllenhaal. Her other recent film credits include “Ladies First,” “Now You See Me: Now You Don’t” and “Hallow Road.” In 2027, she will reunite with Ritchie for “Wife and Dog,” which also stars Anthony Hopkins and Benedict Cumberbatch. 

	Headland has been out of the director’s chair ever since helming the short-lived Disney+ series “The Acolyte.” Before that, she directed series such as “Single Drunk Female,” “Almost Family” and “Black Monday.” Her last feature directorial credit was all the way back in 2015 with “Sleeping with Other People.” Coming up, she has “Cult of Love,” a Christmas family dramedy currently in pre-production. 

	Rosamund Pike is repped by CAA, United Agents and Magnolia Entertainment; Leslye Headland is repped by CAA and Sugar23; Daniella Isaacs is repped by Curtis Brown Group.

title: L.A. District Attorney Nathan Hochman Rips Gavin Newsom For Commuting Death Sentences
description:
L.A. D.A. to Gavin Newsom
                          Your Commutations Won't Kill the Death Penalt
body:
L.A. D.A. to Gavin Newsom
                          Your Commutations Won't Kill the Death Penalty
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Gavin Newsom is sparing hundreds of inmates from execution in California ... but Los Angeles County's top prosecutor says the governor can't wipe out the death penalty entirely.
      
    
            In a statement Thursday, District Attorney Nathan Hochman acknowledged Newsom has the constitutional power to commute death sentences ... but stressed, "That power does not extend to eliminating the death penalty."
      
    
    
              
                
  
    
            Hochman pointed out California voters have twice rejected efforts to eliminate the death penalty ... pointing out only voters or the state Legislature can change that law.
      

            Hochman's not backing down ... saying his office will continue considering the death penalty in all eligible cases as long as it remains legal.
      
    
            He also turned his attention to victims' families ... saying they deserve a justice system that honors the law and treats their cases fairly.
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported ... Newsom announced plans Thursday to commute the sentences of all 548 California death row inmates to life in prison without parole, arguing state-sanctioned executions are incompatible with California's values.
      
    
            But there's a catch ... hundreds of those commutations still need approval from the California Supreme Court, and the death penalty itself remains on the books.

title: Russell Brand Looking at 6 to 9 Years Behind Bars, Bar Council Chair Says
description:
Russell Brand
                          Could Be Looking at 6 to 9 Years in Jail
body:
Russell Brand
                          Could Be Looking at 6 to 9 Years in Jail
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 5, 2026
                            5:51 PM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Russell Brand may be locked up for quite a while ... at least what the chair of the Bar Council says.
      
    
            Kirsty Brimelow told Sky News the actor was looking at "between six and nine years" in prison for his crimes.
      
    
            As we previously reported, the actor was convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault on Thursday.
      

            He was denied bail and will remain behind bars until his sentencing on Monday.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Brand was acquitted of two other rape charges and attempted indecent assault ... but a detective who oversaw his investigation believes he's still a danger to women.
      
    
            The detective said that between Brand's "position of power and trust" and his "millions of followers," he remains a risk.

title: Miss USA CEO Slams Dethroned Miss North Carolina in Lawsuit Over Racial Slur Usage
description:
Miss USA
                          Slams Dethroned Miss North Carolina ...
body:
Miss USA
                          Slams Dethroned Miss North Carolina ...
                          You Can't Sue, You Admitted Using Racial Slur!!!
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The Miss USA organization and its CEO are firing back at former Miss North Carolina USA, Brittany Boltinhouse, who is suing after she was stripped of her crown ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            In court docs, obtained by TMZ, Miss USA's leader, Thom Brodeur, slammed Brittany's lawsuit, in which she claimed the pageant execs defamed her.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Thom and the organization argued their public statements about the matter didn't defame Brittany. They claim the statement did not name Brittany … and say, even if they did, it would still be an expression of opinion … and you can't sue someone for defamation over stating their opinion.
      
    
            Miss USA and Thom also insist Brittany already admitted to using racist slurs in social media posts … and therefore her lawsuit is nonsense.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Brittany was named Miss North Carolina in June 2026 and was scheduled to compete in the Miss USA pageant in August 2026 ... but the organization pulled Brittany from the competition after old social media posts where she used the n-word surfaced.
      
    
            Brittany claimed Miss USA also removed her due to her attending President Trump's rally on January 6, 2021, posting about the Tate brothers, and posting a tribute for Charlie Kirk.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The pageant released a statement announcing Brittany was being removed. It also said, "The organization said it does not tolerate racism, homophobia, transphobia, nor language that strips any person of their dignity." Brittany didn't take issue with her being taken out of the competition, but felt the statement created a false public narrative that she was a racist.
      
    
            Brittany has yet to respond to the latest filing.

title: Dolly Parton's Manager Voluntarily Dismisses Lawsuit Against Her Nephew
description:
Dolly Parton's Manager
                          Dismisses Lawsuit Against Her Nephew
body:
Dolly Parton's Manager
                          Dismisses Lawsuit Against Her Nephew
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
          Update
  
    
            3:34 PM PT -- Bryan Seaver's attorney, Dominic J. Leonardo, tells TMZ ... "Mr. Seaver cares deeply about his Aunt Dolly, her music, her family, and the incredible legacy she left behind. He has made a career out of protecting his aunt while she was alive and remains committed to Dolly and his entire family. Mr. Seaver is grateful to put this misunderstanding behind him so that the entire family can continue to grieve peacefully and ensure that the bright light of Dolly's legacy remains entirely untouched."
      
    
            Dolly Parton's nephew Bryan Seaver just scored a major legal victory ... because the late legend's manager has dropped the lawsuit against him.
      
    
            According to Rolling Stone, Danny Nozell filed a notice of voluntary dismissal of his lawsuit Thursday ... in the suit, Danny alleged Bryan had threatened Dolly's business empire.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The dismissal comes before a hearing scheduled for Tuesday ... and before Danny needed to respond to Bryan's denial of the allegations.
      

            It's unclear why Danny pulled the plug on the suit ... or if he and Bryan reached a settlement.
      
    
    
              
                
  
    
            As we previously reported ... Dolly's nephew asked the judge to dismiss the case against him ... claiming he'd never threatened Danny and the texts he'd sent him had been in jest.
      
    
            Bryan's not completely out of the woods ... Danny dismissed the lawsuit without prejudice ... meaning it could be brought again.
      
    
            Stay tuned ...
